chapter: Basie and life on the road
title: The Uncle Tom story at the Famous Door
summary: Defines Uncle Tom, and tells of a woman following him from Bourbon Street and being beaten by white men.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, you know like, there, I know you've heard the expression, Uncle Tom. Sure. And I tell people I've only known Uncle Tom once in my life.
Explain what you mean by Uncle Tom, because I've, I've heard, you know, I've heard the expression. Yeah, Uncle Tom.

Did you ever, did you ever see Uncle Tom's cabin? Sure, sure. Well, Uncle Tom is a, a, a, a black person who'd do anything to get along with a white person, or try to keep him happy. Oh, okay. Yeah. Say things to make him laugh, or, like, some guys, the guy said, you know like, he'd tell a white guy, tell a, a sad joke. Mm-hmm.
And Uncle Tom, ah, man, you so funny. Exactly.
Yeah. So the only time I ever had Uncle Tom in my life, I was working at the famous door.

And Lord and Miss Claudia had just come out, and I sang Lord and Miss Claudia, and Miss Woman kept sending me five dollar bills up there to sing Lord and Miss Claudia. And when the thing was over, I was walking towards Canal Street to catch the bus, because I didn't have, I didn't have a car at the time. So I heard somebody behind, walking behind me. She said, hey, wait a minute. Wait a minute. I knew there was nobody, because there didn't have any black women on Bourbon Street at the time. The only black people would be following on Bourbon Street was people who worked there, like the maids or the butlers or musicians, you know. So I, when she said, hey, trumpet player, when she said trumpet player, she said, wait a minute, wait a minute. So I started walking faster. And she started walking faster. And I didn't want to run, because the first thing somebody, a cop probably would have shot me and said, this black guy snatched this woman's pocketbook.

So I just walked fast. So she finally caught up with me at Canal and Bourbon. That's where the bus was going to stop. She said, come on, come on. I said, miss, will you please leave me alone? And just at that time, they had about three big white guys, looked like football players, a wrestler. One of them looked like he was as big as Hulk Hogan. So he said, what's wrong, what's wrong? They thought I was messing with the women. She said, I said, miss, I said, would you please leave me alone? I said, I don't like you white women. I want my own colored women. So the guy stood and she said, come on, the guy said, what's wrong? She said, ain't nothing wrong, I'm just trying to get him to go out with me. Man, oh three guys whipped that woman.

That's what's wrong now. Y'all don't be, them so and so, the ends don't be running behind, you'll be running behind the men's. They didn't worry, you know. Say, hey man, so while they was whipping me, I saw a cab, I got in the cab. And men, but they gave her a good working, working over.
So that was the only time? Yeah.

It was timing Uncle Tom then. Because those guys, man, see at that time I was weighing about a hundred and forty-two pounds. And these guys weighed well over three hundred, there were three of them. And there was nobody around, it was about three o'clock in the morning. But they put a whipping on her.
